title: Nasruddin and the Eagle
summary: Nasruddin had never seen an eagle before. Finding a wounded golden eagle on the mountain crags, he brought it home....
full_text:
Nasruddin had never seen an eagle before. Finding a wounded golden eagle on the mountain crags, he brought it home.

"Heavens!" cried Nasruddin. "What a neglected bird! Your beak is curved like a sickle, your claws are sharp as needles, and your feathers are wild and unruly!"

He took large shears, trimmed the eagle's magnificent hooked beak straight, cut its mighty talons blunt, and combed its feathers flat.

He stroked the bird with satisfaction: "There now! You look like a proper, respectable domestic pigeon!"
moral: Forcing wild magnificence into ordinary domestic molds destroys its beauty.
